Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010, as amended by Real Decreto 389/2021, de 1 de junio, establishing the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual or serviced office address is generally acceptable for registration purposes provided the SL has a genuine Spanish address for notifications and correspondence. However, Spanish corporate law (Article 9, Ley de Sociedades de Capital) requires the registered office to coincide with the place of effective management or principal establishment. Notaries and the Commercial Registry may request proof that the registered office is not fictitious. For a voice-streaming app relying on Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, a pure virtual-office arrangement without any domestic employees, management, billing records, or tax substance is likely to be challenged in a bank account application, UBO registry filing, or AEAT tax inspection. Virtual office is therefore permissible only as a gateway to a substantive Spanish operational address.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, under the supervision of the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act, particularly Articles 4, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 30, 32, 33, 62, 63, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 225 and 249, as applicable to a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada.

Formation / constitutional filings

Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), followed by registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry. The deed incorporates the articles of association and the founding shareholders' subscription declarations.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 45 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum capital of an SL is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation; no general escrow account is legally mandatory, although banks commonly issue a capital deposit certificate. If capital is below EUR 3,000, the company is subject to the statutory legal-reserve and shareholder-liability safeguards in Article 4 of the Companies Act until the required threshold is reached.

Funding & unlock path: No special industrial clearance is ordinarily required for a software company. Physical premises remain subject to municipal fire-safety and activity requirements, including evacuation routes, emergency planning, fire-protection systems and, where applicable, technical building-code compliance. Structural load inspections are required where equipment, server racks or alterations affect the building. Workplace risk assessment, occupational health arrangements and employee safety training are required under Spanish occupational-risk legislation.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum capital of an SL is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation; no general escrow account is legally mandatory, although banks commonly issue a capital deposit certificate. If capital is below EUR 3,000, the company is subject to the statutory legal-reserve and shareholder-liability safeguards in Article 4 of the Companies Act until the required threshold is reached.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED: The Company accepts and confirms the subscriptions and full payment of the quotas set out in the deed of incorporation and articles of association. The registered office is adopted at the address specified in the deed, with authority granted to update it in the Mercantile Registry. [Name] is appointed sole director, or the directors identified in the deed are appointed to their respective offices, each accepting the appointment and declaring eligibility. The officers are authorized to obtain tax, banking, electronic-signature, municipal and operational registrations, execute ancillary documents, and take all lawful actions necessary to commence the Company’s business.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

Not applicable for the stated digital application activity. If physical technical installations, telecommunications equipment, or regulated premises are operated, the competent authority is the relevant autonomous-community industry department and the municipality where the premises are located.

Category: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required for an interactive audio chatroom and companion social application. A municipal prior communication or activity declaration may be required for offices, studios, customer premises, or other physical facilities.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica, www.agenciatributaria.es

E-government filing portal

For an ES SL: (1) obtain provisional corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from AEAT using Modelo 036 after the articles of association are executed and before/within registration; (2) after registration in the Registro Mercantil, request the definitive NIF (Modelo 036/037); (3) register in the Spanish Business Census (Censo de empresarios) simultaneously, thereby obtaining a VAT identification number (NIF-IVA); (4) a Spanish-resident SL is statutorily a taxable person under IVA from day one with no economic turnover threshold; (5) non-resident shareholders require an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) before the notary; a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment must obtain a non-resident NIF via a tax representative (Modelo 030) and, if making distance B2C sales to Spanish customers, may register for IVA through the OSS/IOSS scheme.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — For an ES SL: (1) obtain provisional corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from AEAT using Modelo 036 after the articles of association are executed and before/within registration; (2) after registration in the Registro Mercantil, request the definitive NIF (Modelo 036/037); (3) register in the Spanish Business Census (Censo de empresarios) simultaneously, thereby obtaining a VAT identification number (NIF-IVA); (4) a Spanish-resident SL is statutorily a taxable person under IVA from day one with no economic turnover threshold; (5) non-resident shareholders require an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) before the notary; a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment must obtain a non-resident NIF via a tax representative (Modelo 030) and, if making distance B2C sales to Spanish customers, may register for IVA through the OSS/IOSS scheme.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime; an SL is automatically classified as a resident corporation for income tax and as a taxable person for VAT, with no entity classification election. Applicable statutory elections include: (i) Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) selection for intra-EU B2C distance sales and e-services; (ii) Non-Union OSS for certain B2C digital services to Spanish consumers by non-EU suppliers; (iii) monthly VAT filing option (Modelo 308) rather than quarterly; (iv) optional VAT fiscal group treatment (grupo de entidades, Art. 9.3 LIVA) where a controlling interest exists; and (v) obligatory, non-elective documentation and tax treatment for hybrid-mismatch transactions under ATAD/ATAD II, with no check-the-box variant available.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No de minimis economic-turnover threshold for an established Spanish SL; registration is compulsory before any taxable supply in the Spanish territory. For non-established foreign suppliers of cross-border B2C digital services (including voice-streaming apps), Spain imposes no separate national turnover threshold either. Under the EU Union OSS, an EU-established business remains taxable in its State of establishment for intra-EU supplies until annual cross-border distance sales of goods and e-services to consumers exceed EUR 10,000 (excluding VAT), at which point registration in the customer State becomes mandatory and the OSS election is the statutory mechanism.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

For goods physically exported from the Spanish customs territory to a third country, zero-rating (exención plena, with right to deduction) applies under Art. 21 LIVA where the exporter proves the definitive exit of the goods and retains the customs export declaration and transport documentation. For the voice-streaming/e-digital services of an ES SL: (a) B2B services supplied to a non-resident entrepreneur established outside Spain are zero-rated where that customer is established outside the Tax Administration Area and the service is not used in Spain, evidenced by the customer's foreign VAT registration number or certificate of fiscal residence; (b) B2C electronically supplied services (audio streaming, social audio functions) follow the place-of-supply B2C rule — for consumers established outside the EU/Spain the supply is situated outside the Spanish VAT territory and may be issued without IVA, with two non-contradictory proofs (e.g., IP address, billing address, bank card data, pre-paid SIM registration); (c) intra-EU B2C supplies are taxable in the recipient's EU Member State under the Union OSS once the EU-wide EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold is exceeded; below that threshold, the Spanish SL may retain charging Spanish IVA at 21% unless the OSS election is made.

  • Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / DUDA file)
  • Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical exit from the EU customs territory
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank credit confirmation
  • Commercial invoice marked 'IVA NO DEVENGADO — ART.21 LIVA' or place-of-supply substantiation
  • Transport contract (CMR, POD) and Incoterms® 2020 terms confirming risk transfer
  • Export license or authorized exporter status document where applicable
  • For digital e-services: IP-address logs, geolocation data, customer residence certificate, payment gateway billing address, and device/phone registration records proving the customer's place of supply outside Spain/EU

Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-stamping/clearance system analogous to Italy's SdI, but the following electronic fiscal controls apply: (1) the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires taxpayers with annual turnover above EUR 6,000,000, VAT groups, monthly-refund registrants and certain consortia to transmit invoice and received-invoice data to AEAT within 4 calendar days; (2) under Real Decreto 1007/2023 (Verifactu), billing software and workflows must be certified to ensure invoice authenticity, integrity, legibility and immediate transmission of records to AEAT upon request; (3) the 'Crea y Crece' law mandates interoperable B2B e-invoicing (Facturae or equivalent) between entrepreneurs and professionals once the relevant final implementation order is issued, with a transition scheme; (4) self-issued invoices (e.g., reverse-charge calls) remain subject to the same integrity rules, and the Basque Country/Navarra foral territories operate TicketBai/TaxBAI real-time invoice declaration systems.

If a zero-rated export transaction is not properly substantiated within the four-year statutory documents-retention period (Arts. 70 and 112 LGT; Art. 114 LIVA and RD 1624/1992), AEAT will retroactively assess IVA at the applicable rate (currently 21%) plus default interest from the original invoice date. Tax penalties under LGT Arts. 191–193 range from 50% to 150% of the amount evaded in the case of false or inaccurate zero-rating; where the fraudulent export scheme causes aggregate tax damage exceeding EUR 120,000, it may constitute a criminal offence under Criminal Code Art. 305, carrying imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of two to six times the defrauded amount. AEAT's SII/Verifactu real-time audit capabilities and cross-matching with consignment records in EU customs databases mean any artificial or unsupported export substantiation triggers immediate clawbacks, exclusion from the quarterly/monthly VAT refund system, and coordinated civil/criminal enforcement.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain operates within the European Economic Area and the eurozone, with full current-account and capital-account convertibility for resident and non-resident entities. No prior administrative authorization is required for capital movements to or from EU/EEA member states. For transactions with non-EU jurisdictions, only statistical reporting (declaraciones informativas) and, where applicable, anti-money laundering declarations are required for amounts exceeding €50,000 or under other threshold rules. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject to corporate income tax withholding recovery or treaty relief, and supported by proof of tax residence and beneficial ownership documentation.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion rule for export proceeds in Spain. Receipts in foreign currency may be retained, converted freely, or credited to external accounts at market rates. Under Royal Decree 2071/1998 and Banco de España Circular rules, resident companies must file balance-of-payments statistical declarations for transactions exceeding €50,000 (or equivalent), including export/import payments, but no mandatory timeline for repatriation or conversion ratio applies.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMI) may passport into Spain under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and can provide multi-currency IBANs, virtual accounts, and cross-border liquidity rails. Non-EU fintech/EMIs without a licence, branch, or appointed agent in Spain cannot lawfully onboard a Spanish SL as a primary payments counterparty or provide unregulated escrow services. Due diligence stronger in practice on fintechs without full banking licence; a Tier-1 Spanish bank or an EU banking-licensed institution with a Spanish branch is recommended for capital escrow and settlement accounts.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident corporate directors and ultimate beneficial owners domiciled in jurisdictions with opaque ownership registries

Root cause: Non-resident corporate directors and ultimate beneficial owners domiciled in jurisdictions with opaque ownership registries

Defense evidence: Apostilled certificate of incorporation, current registry of beneficial owners (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada public deed), identification of every UBO with passport copies and utility bills, notarised power of attorney in Spanish, and a written explanation of the commercial substance of voice streaming operations in Spain.
High-volume microtransactions from digital platforms (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) flagged as potential fungible value transfer

Root cause: High-volume microtransactions from digital platforms (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) flagged as potential fungible value transfer

Defense evidence: Audited platform revenue reports, contractual agreements with app stores, a recurring AML operational policy addressing app-store deduction reconciliation, transaction monitoring logs, and a cash-flow projection demonstrating expected settlement cycles and refund rules.
Ownership concentration and crypto-asset or fintech legacy exposure in the shareholder chain

Root cause: Ownership concentration and crypto-asset or fintech legacy exposure in the shareholder chain

Defense evidence: Independent source-of-wealth report, audited financial statements of shareholders, exchange and fintech transaction history showing provenance of injected capital, and a sworn declaration of no sanctioned activities with supporting sanctions screening certificates from a reputable screening provider.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Inbound equity injections to the Spanish SL are executed via SWIFT MT103 with clear narrative reference 'Capital Sustantivo / Inversión Extranjera' and the relevant Banco de España balance-of-payments statistical purpose code (e.g., 'Inversión directa de no residente en entidades residentes'). The routing must include a valid Spanish IBAN (ES-code), the SL's tax ID (CIF/NIF), and the reference to the notarial deed and registry appointment (nombramiento). Funds originating from outside the EU may require additional supporting documents: apostilled source of funds disclosure, proof of beneficial owner identity, and the Escritura de Constitución. Amounts above €1 million or with high-risk origins may trigger enhanced due diligence and a potential hold pending review by the bank's compliance department.Operational and trade-related outflows are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for standard invoice settlements, licensing fees, infrastructure costs, and contractor payments. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) are used where counterparties demand documentary instruments against shipment or services; the Spanish SL's account bank will require the underlying commercial contract, invoice, bill of lading or proof-of-service, and any relevant compliance annex. SEPA (SCT and SDD Core) rails are available for beneficiary accounts in the EU/EEA, and instant payment (SCT Inst) can be used for high-velocity low-value settlements, though Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds arrive via platform remittances using SWIFT or local automated clearing house (ACH) equivalents, typically in EUR.Plain vanilla EUR/Foreign Currency ForwardsOutright FX swaps (swap de divisas)Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for inconvertible or thinly traded emerging-market currenciesEUR/USD and EUR/LATAM currency options (call/spread) for hedging receivables from Latin American marketsCross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for non-EUR debt refinancingCurrency futures traded on regulated EU exchanges (e.g., Eurex) or OTC with qualified bank counterparties

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMI) may passport into Spain under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and can provide multi-currency IBANs, virtual accounts, and cross-border liquidity rails. Non-EU fintech/EMIs without a licence, branch, or appointed agent in Spain cannot lawfully onboard a Spanish SL as a primary payments counterparty or provide unregulated escrow services. Due diligence stronger in practice on fintechs without full banking licence; a Tier-1 Spanish bank or an EU banking-licensed institution with a Spanish branch is recommended for capital escrow and settlement accounts.

Annual Financial Statements (Cuentas Anuales) – approval and deposit For 31 December year-end: shareholders' approval by 30 June; deposit at the Commercial Registry within one month from approval, i.e. by 31 July. $0 USD Fine of EUR 200 to EUR 300,000 under the ICAC late-filing regime; Commercial Registry file closure (cierre registral) until accounts and audit report (if applicable) are deposited.

Annual Beneficial-Ownership (UBO) Update/Confirmation Embedded in the annual accounts deposit due by 31 July; any change in the beneficial-ownership structure must be notified within 10 business days of the corporate event. $0 USD Penalties under Spain's AML Law 10/2010 (up to EUR 600,000 for serious infringements) and blocking of further Mercantile Registry filings until the UBO declaration is updated.

For 31 December year-end: shareholders' approval by 30 June; deposit at the Commercial Registry within one month from approval, i.e. by 31 July.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% for beneficiaries resident in EU/EEA states (or with treaty entitlement); 24% generally for non-residents without treaty/EU status; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate holdings (≥5% for ≥12 months).

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 days and 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (i.e., by 25 July for calendar year-end entities).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 100 Net accounting result (resultado contable) before statutory adjustments. Report the company's P&L result; no direct remittance effects. Late filing without prior request triggers surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 10% within 6 months, 15% between 6 and 12 months, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Filing a false or incomplete return is a serious infringement: administrative penalties from 75% to 150% of the tax loss or, in absence of loss, fixed penalties from €200 to €600; potential criminal referral if the amount exceeds €120,000.

Late filing without prior request triggers surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 10% within 6 months, 15% between 6 and 12 months, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Filing a false or incomplete return is a serious infringement: administrative penalties from 75% to 150% of the tax loss or, in absence of loss, fixed penalties from €200 to €600; potential criminal referral if the amount exceeds €120,000.

Filing a false or incomplete return is a serious infringement: administrative penalties from 75% to 150% of the tax loss or, in absence of loss, fixed penalties from €200 to €600; potential criminal referral if the amount exceeds €120,000.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation is required if net turnover exceeds EUR 10 million, or if related-party transactions with any single counterparty exceed EUR 250,000 in a tax year. Country-by-country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not impose Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, substance principles are embedded in the GAAR (Article 15 LIS), the Spanish ETVE privileged regime (EC Decision of EU), the participation exemption (5% holding, ≥1-year holding, no asset-driven tax avoidance), and financing/treaty claims. Lack of economic substance can trigger recharacterisation, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate Income Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalty of 75%–150% of the loss; criminal sanction under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code: imprisonment from 1 to 6 years, fine up to six times the evaded amount.

Director personal liability: Directors who authorised or participated are jointly and severally liable under Article 40.2 LGT for unpaid corporate tax and penalties; may face travel bans within Schengen territory and disqualification for company administration.
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: Recharacterisation of the structure by the AEAT; denial of deduction of intra-group payments; penalty of 75%–150% of the reassessed amount; if the artificiality is used to evade tax, criminal exposure under the Criminal Code.

Director personal liability: Directors can be personally liable for the tax debt (Article 42 LGT) and, in serious cases, criminally liable for structuring a sham entity; court may impose 5-year ban on company administration and temporary seizure of property.
AML and Financial Crime Compliance

Statutory sanction: Law 10/2010 penalties: serious violations from €120,000 to €1,500,000; money-laundering criminal offence under Article 301 of the Criminal Code with imprisonment of 1 to 6 years.

Director personal liability: Board members and the appointed compliance officer may be jointly and severally liable for corporate fines; personal interdictions, asset freezes, and European Arrest Warrant arrest for money-laundering participation.
Transfer Pricing Non-Disclosure

Statutory sanction: Specific penalty under the LGT: up to 15% of the amount of related-party operations (5% if conformed promptly); a secondary adjustment can trigger an additional corporate tax assessment of 75%–150%.

Director personal liability: Directors who sign, or direct the preparation of, the flawed return are jointly liable for the penalty under Articles 42 and 44 LGT and may also face criminal consequences for fraudulent tax filings.
